items.entity: design domain (16 × 32 grid) orientation relative to the cantilever axis
items.description: Sec. 4 and the Abstract give only '16 × 32 square elements' with a 'cantilever' boundary condition. The text does not say which element count runs along the span (support to load) and which through the depth; only Figs. 10–11 show this. 'Cantilever beam' (Sec. 6) suggests the longer side is the span, but this is not definitive.
readings: span 32 elements (horizontal) × depth 16 elements (nelx = 32, nely = 16; 2:1 cantilever)
span 16 elements × depth 32 elements (nelx = 16, nely = 32; deep 1:2 cantilever)

items.entity: physical element size and out-of-plane thickness
items.description: Sec. 4 gives only element counts and says the unit was omitted. Element side length and plate thickness are never stated. For 2D square elements the compliance does not depend on element size and scales with 1/thickness.
readings: unit square elements (domain 32 × 16 length units), unit thickness
other element size / thickness (rescales compliance only)

items.entity: cantilever support (which edge, what extent)
items.description: Sec. 4 says only 'As the boundary condition, we choose the cantilever', and Sec. 6 says 'cantilever beam'. Neither names the supported edge or how much of it is fixed, and no boundary-condition figure is referenced.
readings: entire end edge x = 0 (all nodes) fixed, with the load on the opposite end x = L (fixing x = L instead is the mirror image)
only a central portion of the end edge fixed (partial clamp)

items.entity: constrained DOFs at the cantilever support
items.description: 'Cantilever' implies a built-in end, but Sec. 4 never says which displacement components are fixed at the support nodes.
readings: fully clamped: u_x = u_y = 0 at every node of the supported edge
u_x = 0 at all supported-edge nodes and u_y = 0 at a single node (e.g., mid-node)

items.entity: tip load on the free end
items.description: Sec. 4 gives no load point, only 'cantilever'. Usual cantilever benchmarks put the load at mid-depth or at a corner of the free edge.
readings: free end edge at 0.5 of the depth (mid-depth node)
free end edge at a corner, 0.0 of the depth (bottom; the top corner at 1.0 gives the mirror image)

items.entity: tip load on the free end
items.description: Sec. 4 does not say whether the load is a single nodal force or a distributed traction.
readings: concentrated force at one node
force spread over 2–3 adjacent nodes about the load point
uniform shear traction over the whole free edge

items.entity: tip load on the free end
items.description: Load direction is not stated; Sec. 4 says only 'cantilever'. The usual reading is a load transverse to the beam axis. Up or down does not matter for linear compliance, because compliance and its sensitivities are quadratic in the load.
readings: perpendicular to the beam axis (e.g., vertical −y for a horizontal beam)
inclined tip load with an axial component (e.g., 45°)

items.entity: tip load on the free end
items.description: The load magnitude is never given; Table 3 reports only 'dimensionless compliance'. By my rough beam estimate, a unit load with E0 = 1 and unit thickness on a 32×16 cantilever at x0 = 0.5, p = 3 gives an initial compliance of a few hundred, not the reported 5,974. So the actual load or scaling is uncertain.
readings: F = 1 (unit load)
a non-unit load (or other scaling) chosen to reproduce Table 3's absolute values

items.entity: Poisson's ratio
items.description: Sec. 4 states ν = 1.0, which is impossible for an isotropic linear-elastic material. The plane-stress material matrix, proportional to 1/(1−ν²), becomes singular, and plane strain becomes indefinite. The value is almost certainly a typo or placeholder.

items.entity: 2D constitutive assumption
items.description: The FEM data in Sec. 4 do not say whether the analysis is plane stress or plane strain. This matters whenever ν ≠ 0.
readings: plane stress
plane strain

items.entity: finite-element type for the square elements
items.description: Sec. 2.2.1 and Sec. 4 say only 'square elements' and 'FEM'; element formulation and integration are not given. The shear-locking remark in Sec. 3.2.4 suggests low-order bilinear elements.
readings: 4-node bilinear quadrilateral (Q4), full 2×2 Gauss integration
8-node quadratic quadrilateral (Q8)

items.entity: lower density bound x_min (Eqs. 3–4)
items.description: Sec. 2.2.1 says x_min 'is set to eliminate numerical instability' but gives no value. x_min also sets the void stiffness used when the filtered 0/1 designs in Table 3 are analysed.
readings: x_min = 0.01

items.entity: OC update parameters (move limit m, damping η, λ bisection)
items.description: Eqs. (5)–(6) use a move limit and a damping exponent (m and η in the Nomenclature), but no values are given. The bounds and tolerance of the λ bisection are also unspecified. This applies to both methods.
readings: m = 0.2, η = 0.5 (99-line-code defaults)

items.entity: sensitivity/density (mesh-independence) filter during OC iterations
items.description: Sec. 2.3 lists only floating-island removal and threshold binarization for the previous SIMP method. It never says whether a standard sensitivity or density filter, and its radius, acts inside the OC loop. Typical SIMP codes include one.
readings: no sensitivity/density filter
Sigmund sensitivity filter, rmin = 1.5 elements
density filter, rmin = 1.5–2 elements

items.entity: OC termination criterion
items.description: Sec. 2.4 step 5 says to iterate 'until the difference between x_new and x falls below a certain value', with no tolerance given. Table 2 and the Fig. 11 caption instead report a fixed 40 density updates for both methods.
readings: stop after exactly 40 OC updates
stop when max|x_new − x| < 0.01
stop at max|Δx| < 0.01 or 40 updates, whichever comes first

items.entity: initial uniform density x0
items.description: Sec. 4 says only 'evenly distributed density over the design area (see Fig. 10)'; the value is shown only in Fig. 10. Table 3 (initial 5,974 vs. SIMP 1,294) fits x0 = 0.5 with p = 3: the initial design is 8× the full-solid compliance and the optimum about 1.7×. Table 3 also rules out x0 ≳ 0.6, since a 50% design cannot be stiffer than the full solid.
readings: x0 = 0.5 everywhere (equal to the volume limit)
another uniform value below about 0.6 (e.g., 0.4)

items.entity: binarization threshold θ in Eq. (7), previous method
items.description: Sec. 2.3 sets θ only indirectly, 'so that the total volume' matches that of the proposed method's result. Neither θ nor the resulting volume is reported.
readings: θ such that the binarized SIMP design has exactly 50% volume (256 of 512 elements)
θ matching the unreported solid-element count of the proposed method's filtered design

items.entity: timing of threshold/island filtering in the previous method
items.description: Sec. 2.4 applies Eq. (7) and island removal once, to the converged solution (step 6). Sec. 5.2.1, however, blames a compliance increase around update 30 in Fig. 13(b) on the filtering, which implies filtering during the iterations.
readings: filters applied once after the final (40th) update
filters applied at every update and fed back into the next OC step
filtered design evaluated at every update only for reporting compliance, not fed back

items.entity: floating-island removal (Sec. 2.3, Sec. 3.2.4.1)
items.description: Islands are defined only as material 'not connected to any other elements regarded as material'. The text does not say whether edge or corner contact counts as connected, or whether whole clusters cut off from the main structure are removed.
readings: remove solid elements with no edge-sharing solid neighbour (4-connectivity)
remove solid elements with no solid element among the 8 surrounding ones
remove every solid cluster not connected to the main support-to-load structure

items.entity: small-hole filling (proposed method, Sec. 3.2.4.2)
items.description: Sec. 3.2.4.2 says only that holes 'with sizes larger than a certain size are not excluded'. Three things are never quantified: the size limit, how a hole's cells are judged connected, and the checkerboard check that decides whether to fill (Sec. 3.2.4).
readings: always fill enclosed void clusters of 1 element
always fill enclosed void clusters of ≤ 4 elements (2×2)
fill holes of ≤ 2 elements only when a checkerboard pattern is detected

items.entity: peninsula removal and order of filter operations (Sec. 3.2.4.3)
items.description: The rule is given: remove a solid element with ≤ 2 solid elements among its 8 neighbours. Not stated: how boundary and support elements are treated, whether the pass repeats until nothing changes, and the order of the island, hole and peninsula steps.
readings: single pass, out-of-domain neighbours counted as void, order islands→holes→peninsulas
repeat until no change, out-of-domain neighbours counted as void
out-of-domain neighbours counted as solid (edge elements protected)

items.entity: post-processing workflow and binarization of the proposed method
items.description: Sec. 3.2.3 applies the filtering 'with the optimum structure generated by the CNN as the initial structure', which suggests further optimization starting from the CNN result. Sec. 3.2 step 6 just says 'Apply filtering'. The threshold for turning the CNN result into 0/1 before these filters is never given; θ in Eq. (7) is defined only for the previous method.
readings: binarize the 40th-update CNN–OC result at 0.5, then apply the three filters once
use the CNN result as the initial design for further OC updates, applying the filters at each update
binarize to exactly 50% volume, then apply the filters

items.entity: volume of the final filtered designs (Fig. 11(b),(d); Table 3)
items.description: The 50% upper limit in Sec. 4 governs the OC iterations. But Sec. 3.2.4 admits that hole filling breaks the mass constraint (Appendix 1 says the area 'remarkably increases'), and θ is tuned to match volumes. So the final volumes behind the Table 3 compliances are not reported.
readings: exactly 50% (256 of 512 elements)
above 50% by an unreported amount after hole filling
equal for both methods at an unreported value set via θ

items.entity: CNN sensitivity surrogate – training data (Sec. 3.2.1)
items.description: Sec. 3.2.1 omits several things: the number of training samples and the bar-system parameters (number of bars, width and endpoint ranges). It also omits the support and load points the bars connect, the boundary conditions and SIMP parameters (p, x_min) used for the FEM sensitivities, and any output normalization. These are needed to reproduce Fig. 11(c),(d).
readings: random 0/1 bar-system layouts on the same 16×32 grid under the same cantilever boundary conditions, with FEM sensitivities at p = 3 and x_min for voids
as above, but also including intermediate-density samples

items.entity: CNN sensitivity surrogate – architecture, training and network instance
items.description: Table 1 lists only strides and channel counts. Missing are kernel sizes, padding, activations, the output size of the final fully connected layer, the loss function, batch size, epochs and weight initialization/seed. The paper also does not say which trained network (CNN 1 or CNN 2 of Fig. 14) produced Fig. 11, and Sec. 5.3.2 shows that retraining changes the layout.
readings: 3×3 flat convolutions, 3×3 stride-2 down-convolutions (5×5 for the first), 4×4 stride-½ up-convolutions, ReLU, MSE loss, final fully connected layer to 512 outputs
3×3 kernels throughout, ReLU, MSE loss, no output normalization

locator: Sec. 4, the example for performance verification (Fig. 11)
